tvs.title_bl1_about: Have you already booked your eyebrow, eye or lip micropigmentation touch-up?
tvs.text_bl1_about: Don't miss this opportunity. In fact, the tattoo touch-up is always considered the second mandatory and important stage of every micropigmentation procedure. Although a touch-up takes no more than 30–60 minutes, the result exceeds all expectations. The touch-up doesn't just finish your brow, lip or eye tattoo – it adds color, depth of shade and shape, and eliminates any imperfections that may appear while the skin regenerates. The touch-up definitely extends the effect, since the pigment is placed in the skin again during the procedure. So, thanks to the touch-up, your tattoo will last six months or even a year longer.

tvs.title-bl-seo: The importance and specifics of a tattoo touch-up
tvs.text-bl-seo: Many women skip the semi-permanent makeup touch-up because they find the healed result completely satisfying. But after 6 months or a year, the effect fades noticeably, which can be upsetting and may lead them to think the artist wasn't professional enough or used low-quality supplies. In reality, the true reason is that the touch-up was skipped. The procedure takes half the time and costs 50% of the original price, yet the benefits are three times greater.
tvs.text-bl-seo-2:
Why do you need a tattoo touch-up?

Whatever the technique or the area of micropigmentation, a touch-up offers the following benefits:

  • It corrects minor imperfections – for example, gaps, lighter patches, uneven color or missed spots: any flaws that may appear while the skin heals.
  • It helps refine the shape. For example, brows can be made wider or longer, the lip contour more defined, and the eyeliner longer and more lifted at the top.
  • It brings back the brightness of the shade. During the touch-up, the same shade as before can be used, or you can opt for a slightly more intense color – for example, turn light pink lips into a deep pink or get darker brows.
  • It extends the effect by placing the pigment again. Thanks to the touch-up, your tattoo will last for a good long time.
  • It fully completes the look chosen at the initial procedure. The tattoo takes on its final appearance, and you get to enjoy all its obvious benefits.

When to have a touch-up and how it is done

Right after the first session, the artist picks the most suitable date and books your touch-up. It is usually done 28–35 days after the initial procedure. We recommend sticking to this time frame, as it is considered the best window for a touch-up after micropigmentation.
When you come back to the artist for the touch-up, the procedure is no different from the first one. The only difference is the duration and the intensity of the color work. Most often, if the color doesn't need to change, the artist fills in only the gaps in the micropigmented area to eliminate minor imperfections. But if the entire area needs correcting, the pigment is applied over the whole area. It all depends on the individual situation and is discussed before the touch-up. The artist assesses how your semi-permanent brow, lash line or lip makeup looks and suggests the best solution, so that you ultimately get an excellent, natural result.

How does the skin heal after a touch-up? Does it need special care?

If you had your permanent makeup done at our studio, you already know how quickly and smoothly the skin heals after micropigmentation. We guarantee that healing after a touch-up is practically the same. It also matters how the tattoo is done – whether the entire micropigmented area is worked on or only part of it. Either way, during the touch-up the pigment is placed in the upper layers of the skin, so it is essentially painless, and the skin heals quickly and without complications.
For aftercare, the artist will recommend only chlorhexidine or an equivalent product to disinfect the skin. No special care with various ointments and healing products is needed.

What problems can arise if you skip the permanent makeup touch-up?

As a rule, during eyebrow micropigmentation – especially with the powder technique – the artist places the pigment in the upper layers of the skin. This makes it possible to see how your body absorbs the pigment and what shade it produces. Color retention can be 90–100% or as low as 20%. Before the touch-up, the experienced artist usually assesses how the tattoo looks and places the pigment again, slightly deeper. This method achieves the maximum, natural-looking aesthetic effect. So if you skip the touch-up, the small amount of pigment left in the skin after the first session means the effect will fade from view within 4–6 months.
In fact, the touch-up extends how long the effect lasts. Without it, you can't expect your semi-permanent makeup to last 1.5 to 2 years. This is especially true for people with oily skin: subcutaneous oil rejects and expels the pigment much faster, which is why another touch-up may be needed six months after the previous one.
A tattoo touch-up is considered an inexpensive yet very beneficial and affordable procedure. It is recommended as the essential second micropigmentation session. That way, you'll discover all the advantages of permanent makeup and enjoy them for longer.

migx_questions.questions-text: A touch-up is recommended for all techniques and micropigmented areas. The only exception may be the eye (lash line) tattoo, because it is done with black pigment and is also less exposed to external factors that can make the pigment gradually break down and fade.

migx_questions.questions-title: When is the best time for a lip micropigmentation touch-up?
migx_questions.questions-text: The ideal time for a touch-up is one month after the first session. That is when the skin is considered to have recovered, so the pigment can be placed again. Note that during this period the service costs 50% of the first session price. After that, the touch-up costs 100% of the price of the technique.

migx_questions.questions-title: How much does an eyebrow tattoo touch-up cost?
migx_questions.questions-text: It costs 50% of the first session price if the touch-up is done 30–45 days after the first procedure. After that, the touch-up costs 100% of the price of the technique.

migx_questions.questions-title: How do I know if I need a touch-up?
migx_questions.questions-text: A touch-up is needed if the shape or color of the tattoo needs improving, or if local imperfections need correcting. In any case, even if there is nothing to correct, the touch-up works as “prevention” to keep the effect visible for longer. That said, a touch-up is not mandatory for an eye tattoo, but it is important for powder brows micropigmentation.
